GitHub Actions — .github/workflows/ci.yaml
==========================================

This file is CI for ONE service: product-catalog (Go code under
src/product-catalog). It does not build ads, cart, frontend, or
the rest of the shop.

GitHub reads this YAML on every matching event. You do not run
it on your laptop. Open the repo → Actions → product-catalog-ci.

It works together with:
  src/product-catalog/            Go app + Dockerfile
  kubernetes/productcatalog/deploy.yaml   image: line Argo CD deploys
  argocd/application.yaml         Argo CD app watching kubernetes/
  ghcr.io/oliversims/otel-demo    container registry (your GHCR)


What the whole pipeline is for
------------------------------

Goal: a change to product-catalog source on main becomes a new
container on GHCR, then a git commit that points the Deployment
at that container. Argo CD sees the commit and rolls the pod on
EKS. You never kubectl apply the shop yourself.

  1. Developer changes src/product-catalog and merges to main
  2. GitHub Actions builds/tests the Go app
  3. GitHub Actions builds a linux/amd64 image and pushes GHCR
  4. GitHub Actions commits the new image: tag into deploy.yaml
  5. Argo CD syncs kubernetes/ from main
  6. kubelet on EKS pulls the new tag and starts a new pod


When the workflow runs (the "on:" block)
----------------------------------------

Three ways to start it. Not every way runs every job.

A) pull_request targeting main
   AND the PR touches src/product-catalog/** or this workflow file.

   Jobs that run:  build, code-quality
   Jobs skipped:   docker, updatek8s

   Reason: a PR is not production yet. Do not push an image or
   change main's Deployment until the change is merged.

B) push to main
   AND the commit touches src/product-catalog/**.

   Jobs that run:  build, code-quality, docker, updatek8s

   Changing only kubernetes/productcatalog/deploy.yaml does NOT
   start this workflow. That is on purpose: the last job commits
   that file, and we do not want CI to loop forever.

   Changing only ci.yaml and pushing to main also does NOT start
   the docker/update jobs (push paths are source-only). Use
   workflow_dispatch if you want a full run without changing Go.

C) workflow_dispatch
   You click "Run workflow" in the Actions UI.

   Same jobs as a push to main: build → docker → updatek8s.
   Use this for a first test after linking the GHCR package.


concurrency
-----------

If two runs start for the same git ref (same branch), the newer
one cancels the older one. Stops a pile of overlapping image
builds on a busy branch.


permissions (workflow default)
------------------------------

contents: read

Every job can clone the repo. Jobs that need more (write a
package, push a commit) declare extra permissions locally.
GITHUB_TOKEN is created by GitHub for that run. It is not your
PAT. It expires when the job ends.


Job 1 — build
-------------

Runner: a fresh Ubuntu VM (ubuntu-latest). GitHub Actions VMs
are linux/amd64, same architecture as the EKS t3.medium nodes.

Steps, in order:

  1. actions/checkout@v4
     Clones this repo at the commit that triggered the run.

  2. actions/setup-go@v5
     Installs Go 1.22. Caches modules using
     src/product-catalog/go.sum so later runs are faster.

  3. go mod download && go build
     Compiles main.go to a binary named product-catalog-service.
     That binary is thrown away with the VM. This step only
     proves the code compiles. The real binary that runs in
     Kubernetes is built inside Docker in the docker job.

  4. go test ./...
     Unit tests. If this fails, later jobs that need: build
     never start, so a broken binary is not pushed to GHCR.

This job does NOT talk to Docker or Kubernetes.


Job 2 — code-quality
--------------------

Starts at the same time as build (no needs:). Own VM, own
checkout, own Go install.

  golangci-lint v1.55.2 in src/product-catalog

Style / bug lint. A failure fails the workflow but does not
block docker by itself (docker only needs: build). If you want
lint to gate the image, add  needs: [build, code-quality]  on
the docker job.


Job 3 — docker  (push to main / Run workflow only)
--------------------------------------------------

Skipped on pull_request because of:

  if: github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'

needs: build — waits until compile + tests succeeded.

Extra permission: packages: write  (push to GHCR).

Steps:

  1. checkout again (new VM; nothing is shared from build
     except the "build passed" signal).

  2. Image name (id: meta)
     Builds a unique tag, for example:

       ghcr.io/oliversims/otel-demo:1.12.0-productcatalogservice-1234567890

     github.repository_owner is lowercased (GHCR requires
     lowercase). github.run_id is unique per workflow run.

     Why a new tag every time: Kubernetes imagePullPolicy is
     IfNotPresent. If you overwrite the same tag with different
     bits, a node may keep the old layers. A new tag cannot
     collide with a cached digest. Same lesson as Valkey.

     The image is stored in the existing otel-demo GHCR package
     (many tags, one package). It is not a Docker Hub image.

     The name is written to GITHUB_OUTPUT so the next job can
     read it as needs.docker.outputs.image.

  3. docker/setup-buildx-action
     Buildx can target a platform. We need linux/amd64 so the
     image runs on EKS, even if a future runner were ARM.

  4. docker/login-action
     Registry ghcr.io. Username = github.actor (the user or
     bot that started the run). Password = GITHUB_TOKEN.

     For this login to be allowed to push, the GHCR package
     otel-demo must grant this repository write access:
       GitHub → Packages → otel-demo → Package settings
       → Manage Actions access → this repo, role Write.

     The package should stay Public. EKS nodes have no GitHub
     login. Private packages need an imagePullSecret.

  5. docker/build-push-action
     Context: src/product-catalog
     Dockerfile: src/product-catalog/Dockerfile
     platforms: linux/amd64
     push: true
     tags: the unique name from step 2

     Multi-stage Dockerfile: compile Go in golang:1.22-alpine,
     copy the binary into a small alpine image. That image is
     what the cluster runs.


Job 4 — updatek8s  (push to main / Run workflow only)
-----------------------------------------------------

Skipped on pull_request (same if: as docker).
needs: docker — waits until the image exists on GHCR.

Extra permission: contents: write  (git commit + push).

This job does not talk to the cluster. It only changes git.
Argo CD is what applies YAML to EKS.

Steps:

  1. checkout main (not the triggering SHA)
     ref: main so the image tag is applied on top of the
     latest default branch, not a stale commit.

  2. sed on kubernetes/productcatalog/deploy.yaml
     Replaces only the container image: line that looks like

       image: 'ghcr.io/.../otel-demo:1.12.0-productcatalogservice...'

     with the new unique tag. Comments are left alone.
     grep prints the result so you can see it in the log.

  3. git commit and git push origin HEAD:main
     Author: github-actions[bot] (not a leftover tutorial name).
     Message: ci: point product catalog at <image>

     This is a normal push, not git push -f. Force-push would
     rewrite main history.

     If the file already has that tag, git diff --cached is
     empty and the job exits 0 without a commit.

After this push, Argo CD (application otel-demo, path
kubernetes/, targetRevision main) sees deploy.yaml change and
rolls opentelemetry-demo-productcatalogservice in namespace
otel-demo.


Why this commit does not start CI again
---------------------------------------

on.push.paths is only src/product-catalog/**.

The bot commit touches kubernetes/productcatalog/deploy.yaml.
That path is not in the filter, so GitHub does not start a new
run. No loop.


What this file does NOT do
--------------------------

  - It does not deploy the whole shop (only product-catalog).
  - It does not run terraform / EKS / Argo CD install.
  - It does not kubectl apply. Argo CD does that from git.
  - It does not push to Docker Hub. No DOCKER_USERNAME secret.
  - It does not overwrite tag 1.12.0-productcatalogservice.
  - It does not force-push main.


One-time GitHub setup
---------------------

  1. Packages → otel-demo → Package settings
     → Manage Actions access → this repo → Write.

  2. Keep otel-demo Public so EKS can pull.

  3. Actions tab: product-catalog-ci should appear after this
     file is on main. Use "Run workflow" for a first full run.


How to watch a run
------------------

  GitHub → Actions → product-catalog-ci → the latest run.

  Then on the cluster:

    kubectl get pods -n otel-demo -l app.kubernetes.io/component=productcatalogservice
    kubectl get application otel-demo -n argocd
